John R. Stegner

Independent candidate for Governor, Idaho · Challenger

Retired Idaho Supreme Court justice

John R. Stegner is a retired Idaho Supreme Court justice who spent 25 years as a judge in Idaho, first as a district judge in Latah County starting in 1997 and then on the Supreme Court from 2018 until he retired in 2023. He filed as an independent candidate for governor on February 27, 2026, and the Idaho Secretary of State lists his filing as approved for the November 3, 2026 general election. He formally launched his campaign on July 7, 2026, saying he is running to restore confidence in Idaho government.

Where Stegner stands

Private school choice
Opposes the Idaho Parental Choice Tax Credit (HB 93). Says it is unconstitutional to fund private and homeschool students while public schools are not adequately funded, and says his first act as governor would be to try to challenge it in court.
K-12 education funding
Says Idaho has a "solemn obligation" to fund public schools and that current leaders are not meeting it. Lists fulfilling the constitutional duty to fund public education as one of his top three priorities.
Abortion
Supports Proposition 1, the ballot initiative to restore abortion rights in Idaho, and says he would carry it out if it passes. As a justice in 2023, he wrote that the Idaho Constitution protects a fundamental right to end a pregnancy.
Constitutional amendments
Opposes HJR 4, which would let only the Legislature legalize marijuana or other drugs, and HJR 6, which would make English Idaho's official language. Says he will vote against both.
Nuclear waste and the aquifer
Opposes the agreement to host a federal Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campus that would require Idaho to accept out-of-state spent fuel. Argues Idaho could end up taking far more than a third of the nation's waste unless the plan is stopped now.
Immigration enforcement
Says he would not have signed Idaho's 287(g) agreement with ICE. Argues the agency's conduct, including agents wearing masks and not wearing body cameras, should be reined in before Idaho enters such an agreement.
Public lands
Lists keeping public lands in public hands as one of his top three priorities.
Budget and governing approach
Criticizes the Legislature for cutting taxes and spending and for creating the private school tax credit. Says he would act independently and not give in to outside or political pressure.
Health care access
Lists increasing access to medical care as one of his top three priorities.
